source_excerpt:
Each guard's fail-closed path for an unexpected exception logs it with a
    traceback and raises its refusal from that exception. Every other refusal
    reaching the redactor has no cause or is a guard runner's re-raise of an
    inner refusal (an ``UnsafeSqlError`` or ``RlsError``), so it is logged here.

evidence: rule_sets.py:432-441 _logged_by_guard returns True only when __cause__ is non-None and not UnsafeSqlError/RlsError; RefusalRedactingRunner (466-468) logs at WARNING only when it is False. Each fail-closed path logs warning with exc_info and raises from the unexpected exception: ReadOnlyGuardRunner safety/__init__.py:130-146; RlsGuardRunner 209-224; _refuse_denied_functions 239-248; WholeRowSelectGuardRunner whole_row.py:219-231; relations.verify_base_tables relations.py:125-138. Raw refusals with a non-guard cause (readonly.py:545,552; rls.py:215,246) occur only inside functions called beneath those runners, which re-wrap them with an Unsafe/Rls cause, so the redactor still logs them. RuleSetRefusal paths are logged in rule_sets.py:362-371 and skipped by the redactor (463-465). Claim holds.

verify_hint: Trace a refusal raised outside the runner chain (e.g. run_sql tool argument validation, an error raised as a non-UnsafeSqlError/RlsError such as a ValueError from a guard, or a database error naming a column) to the client text
evidence: factory.py:131-148 composes RefusalRedactingRunner outside ReadOnlyGuardRunner, RlsGuardRunner, RuleSetGuardRunner and WholeRowSelectGuardRunner (and the MySQL runner's verify_base_tables relation check), beneath ResultMaskingRunner. Every failure refuses the statement: :class:`RuleSetRefusal`, whose text

verify_hint: Trace a BaseException not derived from Exception (e.g. RecursionError is Exception; consider asyncio.CancelledError) and a KIND_UNPARSEABLE detail; also check RuleSetRefusal detail containing str(exc) never reaches the client
evidence: RuleSetGuardRunner.run_sql (rule_sets.py:357-374) runs the synchronous _rewrite inside try. A RuleSetRefusal is re-raised (362-364). Any other Exception, including RecursionError and MemoryError, is converted to RuleSetRefusal(KIND_UNCHECKED, ...) (365-371). _rewrite (342-355) maps a missing selection, KeyError and denied-function errors to RuleSetRefusal. _parse (108-128) maps the UnsafeSqlError from parsing to RuleSetRefusal(KIND_UNPARSEABLE, str(exc)), and apply_rule_set (304-316) maps re-parse failures to RuleSetRefusal. RuleSetRefusal.__init__ (98-101) sets the message to REFUSAL_PREFIX + kind, where REFUSAL_PREFIX is 'Refused by the rule set: '. The detail argument goes only to .detail, which is logged at line 363 and never put in str(exc). So str(exc) in the KIND_UNCHECKED and KIND_UNPARSEABLE paths never reaches the client. asyncio.CancelledError (a BaseException) cannot be raised inside the synchronous _rewrite. Cancellation only arises at the await of the inner runner, which is outside the guard's own checks. Failures from the inner runner (database or RLS errors) are not guard failures. RefusalRedactingRunner re-raises RuleSetRefusal unchanged (463-465). The docstring scope at lines 23-25 is the guard's own failures.

claim: ANSI mode is a combination mode; reading @@SESSION.sql_mode returns its expanded flags (REAL_AS_FLOAT, PIPES_AS_CONCAT, ANSI_QUOTES, IGNORE_SPACE, ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY) and the runner only removes HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, leaving ANSI_QUOTES and PIPES_AS_CONCAT, so criterion 14's ANSI outcomes depend on sqlglot's MySQL output being unaffected by those flags.

verify_hint: Check `RULE_SET_REMOVED_SQL_MODES` in factory.py against how sqlglot's MySQL generator writes string literals and the `||` operator
evidence: factory.py:67 RULE_SET_REMOVED_SQL_MODES = {HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE, NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES}; sql_runner.py:126-139 reads @@SESSION.sql_mode, drops only those names (case-insensitive), sets the rest, so ANSI's expanded flags ANSI_QUOTES and PIPES_AS_CONCAT (plus REAL_AS_FLOAT, IGNORE_SPACE, ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY) remain. sqlglot (.venv site-packages, mysql dialect): tokenizer QUOTES=["'", '"'] so a double-quoted token parses as a string literal and is regenerated single-quoted; IDENTIFIERS=[`] so identifiers are backtick-quoted; both are unaffected by ANSI_QUOTES. parsers/mysql.py:91 maps TokenType.DPIPE to exp.Or (DPIPE_IS_STRING_CONCAT=False, dialects/mysql.py:31), and generator.py:4304 writes it as the OR keyword, so PIPES_AS_CONCAT does not change the regenerated SQL. Claim's described dependency on sqlglot output is therefore accurate. I read the code only and ran no sqlglot output.

claim: The logging.getLogger('sqllens.rule_sets').warning call in serve is emitted (logging configured before it) so the warning reaches the server log.
verify_against: serve in cli.py and logging setup
verify_hint: Check where logging.basicConfig/handlers are configured relative to the warning in `serve`

Grep of head src for basicConfig|dictConfig|addHandler|logging.config found no logging configuration anywhere in the repo, so the parenthetical 'logging configured before it' is not literally true.
